"""Machine-verify dossier citations against arXiv metadata.

Two modes:

``fetch``  - query the arXiv API for every arXiv identifier referenced by the
            dossiers (politely: small batches, long pauses, retries on 429) and
            store the authoritative title / first author / year in a lookup file.
``apply``  - compare every dossier paper that carries an arXiv id with the
            lookup and set its ``verification`` field:

            * ``verified``            - title similarity >= 0.85 and year within one
            * ``verified-corrected``  - the id resolves to the same work but title or
                                        year differed; dossier metadata is corrected
            * ``unverified``          - no lookup entry, or the id resolves to a
                                        different work (the stale id is kept in
                                        ``verification_evidence`` for a human to fix)

Usage::

    python tools/verify_arxiv.py fetch   [--lookup PATH]
    python tools/verify_arxiv.py apply   [--lookup PATH] [--dry-run]

Non-arXiv sources (books, blogs, vendor documentation, journal-only papers) are
left ``unverified`` by this tool; they need a human or agent check against the
venue page. The bibliography marks them explicitly.
"""
from __future__ import annotations

import argparse
import difflib
import json
import re
import time
import urllib.error
import urllib.request
import xml.etree.ElementTree as ET
from pathlib import Path

ROOT = Path(__file__).resolve().parents[1]
RESEARCH_DIR = ROOT / "docs" / "research"
DEFAULT_LOOKUP = ROOT / "docs" / "research" / "arxiv_lookup.json"
NS = {"a": "http://www.w3.org/2005/Atom"}
ID_RE = re.compile(r"(\d{4}\.\d{4,5})")


def norm(s: str) -> str:
    s = s.lower().replace("’", "'").replace("‘", "'")
    s = re.sub(r"[^a-z0-9 ]+", " ", s)
    return re.sub(r"\s+", " ", s).strip()


def similarity(a: str, b: str) -> float:
    return difflib.SequenceMatcher(None, norm(a), norm(b)).ratio()


def final_dossiers() -> list[Path]:
    return sorted(p for p in RESEARCH_DIR.glob("*.json") if not p.name.endswith(".draft.json") and p.name != "arxiv_lookup.json")


def paper_arxiv_id(p: dict) -> str | None:
    m = ID_RE.search(p.get("arxiv_id") or "") or re.search(r"arxiv\.org/(?:abs|pdf)/(\d{4}\.\d{4,5})", p.get("url") or "")
    return m.group(1) if m else None


def cmd_fetch(lookup_path: Path, batch_size: int, pause: float) -> None:
    ids: set[str] = set()
    for f in final_dossiers():
        for p in json.loads(f.read_text(encoding="utf-8")).get("papers", []):
            aid = paper_arxiv_id(p)
            if aid:
                ids.add(aid)
    found: dict[str, dict] = json.loads(lookup_path.read_text(encoding="utf-8")) if lookup_path.exists() else {}
    todo = [x for x in sorted(ids) if x not in found]
    print(f"{len(ids)} arXiv ids referenced; {len(found)} already resolved; fetching {len(todo)}")
    for i in range(0, len(todo), batch_size):
        batch = todo[i : i + batch_size]
        url = f"https://export.arxiv.org/api/query?id_list={','.join(batch)}&max_results={len(batch)}"
        data = None
        for attempt in range(5):
            try:
                req = urllib.request.Request(url, headers={"User-Agent": "prebuilt-ai-models-bibliography-check/1.0"})
                with urllib.request.urlopen(req, timeout=90) as r:
                    data = r.read()
                break
            except urllib.error.HTTPError as e:
                wait = 45 * (attempt + 1)
                print(f"  batch {i // batch_size}: HTTP {e.code}; waiting {wait}s")
                time.sleep(wait)
            except Exception as e:  # noqa: BLE001
                print(f"  batch {i // batch_size}: {e}; waiting 30s")
                time.sleep(30)
        if data is None:
            print(f"  batch {i // batch_size}: giving up")
            continue
        root = ET.fromstring(data)
        for entry in root.findall("a:entry", NS):
            m = ID_RE.search(entry.findtext("a:id", default="", namespaces=NS))
            title = re.sub(r"\s+", " ", entry.findtext("a:title", default="", namespaces=NS)).strip()
            if not m or title.lower().startswith("error"):
                continue
            authors = [a.findtext("a:name", default="", namespaces=NS) for a in entry.findall("a:author", NS)]
            found[m.group(1)] = {
                "title": title,
                "first_author": authors[0] if authors else "",
                "n_authors": len(authors),
                "year": entry.findtext("a:published", default="", namespaces=NS)[:4],
            }
        lookup_path.write_text(json.dumps(found, indent=1, ensure_ascii=False), encoding="utf-8")
        print(f"  batch {i // batch_size}: resolved {len(found)} total")
        time.sleep(pause)
    print(f"done: {len(found)} of {len(ids)} resolved -> {lookup_path}")


def cmd_apply(lookup_path: Path, dry_run: bool) -> None:
    lookup: dict[str, dict] = json.loads(lookup_path.read_text(encoding="utf-8"))
    grand = {"verified": 0, "verified-corrected": 0, "unverified-nonarxiv": 0, "unverified-missing": 0, "unverified-mismatch": 0}
    for f in final_dossiers():
        d = json.loads(f.read_text(encoding="utf-8"))
        counts = dict.fromkeys(grand, 0)
        for p in d.get("papers", []):
            aid = paper_arxiv_id(p)
            if not aid:
                p["verification"] = "unverified"
                p.setdefault("verification_evidence", "no arXiv identifier; needs venue-page check")
                counts["unverified-nonarxiv"] += 1
                continue
            rec = lookup.get(aid)
            if rec is None:
                p["verification"] = "unverified"
                p["verification_evidence"] = f"arXiv {aid} not resolved by the metadata lookup"
                counts["unverified-missing"] += 1
                continue
            sim = similarity(p.get("title", ""), rec["title"])
            try:
                year_ok = abs(int(p.get("year") or 0) - int(rec["year"] or 0)) <= 1
            except ValueError:
                year_ok = False
            if sim >= 0.85 and year_ok:
                p["verification"] = "verified"
                p["verification_evidence"] = f"arXiv {aid}: title match {sim:.2f}, year {rec['year']}"
                counts["verified"] += 1
            elif sim >= 0.6:
                changes = []
                if sim < 0.97:
                    changes.append(f"title '{p.get('title')}' -> '{rec['title']}'")
                    p["title"] = rec["title"]
                if not year_ok:
                    changes.append(f"year {p.get('year')} -> {rec['year']}")
                    p["year"] = int(rec["year"])
                p["verification"] = "verified-corrected"
                p["verification_evidence"] = f"arXiv {aid}: " + ("; ".join(changes) or f"title match {sim:.2f}")
                counts["verified-corrected"] += 1
            else:
                p["verification"] = "unverified"
                p["verification_evidence"] = (
                    f"arXiv {aid} resolves to a different work ('{rec['title']}', {rec['year']}); id is probably wrong"
                )
                counts["unverified-mismatch"] += 1
        for k, v in counts.items():
            grand[k] += v
        d["_status"] = (
            "research + completeness critique; arXiv metadata verification applied "
            f"({counts['verified'] + counts['verified-corrected']} of {len(d.get('papers', []))} machine-verified; "
            "non-arXiv sources need a venue-page check)"
        )
        print(f"{f.stem}: {counts}")
        if not dry_run:
            f.write_text(json.dumps(d, indent=1, ensure_ascii=False), encoding="utf-8")
    print("total:", grand)


def main() -> None:
    ap = argparse.ArgumentParser(description=__doc__.split("\n")[0])
    sub = ap.add_subparsers(dest="cmd", required=True)
    f = sub.add_parser("fetch")
    f.add_argument("--lookup", type=Path, default=DEFAULT_LOOKUP)
    f.add_argument("--batch-size", type=int, default=25)
    f.add_argument("--pause", type=float, default=12.0)
    a = sub.add_parser("apply")
    a.add_argument("--lookup", type=Path, default=DEFAULT_LOOKUP)
    a.add_argument("--dry-run", action="store_true")
    args = ap.parse_args()
    if args.cmd == "fetch":
        cmd_fetch(args.lookup, args.batch_size, args.pause)
    else:
        cmd_apply(args.lookup, args.dry_run)


if __name__ == "__main__":
    main()

"""Machine-verify dossier citations against arXiv metadata.

Two modes:

``fetch``  - query the arXiv API for every arXiv identifier referenced by the
            dossiers (politely: small batches, long pauses, retries on 429) and
            store the authoritative title / first author / year in a lookup file.
``apply``  - compare every dossier paper that carries an arXiv id with the
            lookup and set its ``verification`` field:

            * ``verified``            - title similarity >= 0.85 and year within one
            * ``verified-corrected``  - the id resolves to the same work but title or
                                        year differed; dossier metadata is corrected
            * ``unverified``          - no lookup entry, or the id resolves to a
                                        different work (the stale id is kept in
                                        ``verification_evidence`` for a human to fix)

Usage::

    python tools/verify_arxiv.py fetch   [--lookup PATH]
    python tools/verify_arxiv.py apply   [--lookup PATH] [--dry-run]

Non-arXiv sources (books, blogs, vendor documentation, journal-only papers) are
left ``unverified`` by this tool; they need a human or agent check against the
venue page. The bibliography marks them explicitly.
"""
from __future__ import annotations

import argparse
import difflib
import json
import re
import time
import urllib.error
import urllib.request
import xml.etree.ElementTree as ET
from pathlib import Path

ROOT = Path(__file__).resolve().parents[1]
RESEARCH_DIR = ROOT / "docs" / "research"
DEFAULT_LOOKUP = ROOT / "docs" / "research" / "arxiv_lookup.json"
NS = {"a": "http://www.w3.org/2005/Atom"}
ID_RE = re.compile(r"(\d{4}\.\d{4,5})")


def norm(s: str) -> str:
    s = s.lower().replace("’", "'").replace("‘", "'")
    s = re.sub(r"[^a-z0-9 ]+", " ", s)
    return re.sub(r"\s+", " ", s).strip()


def similarity(a: str, b: str) -> float:
    return difflib.SequenceMatcher(None, norm(a), norm(b)).ratio()


def final_dossiers() -> list[Path]:
    return sorted(p for p in RESEARCH_DIR.glob("*.json") if not p.name.endswith(".draft.json") and p.name != "arxiv_lookup.json")


def paper_arxiv_id(p: dict) -> str | None:
    m = ID_RE.search(p.get("arxiv_id") or "") or re.search(r"arxiv\.org/(?:abs|pdf)/(\d{4}\.\d{4,5})", p.get("url") or "")
    return m.group(1) if m else None


def cmd_fetch(lookup_path: Path, batch_size: int, pause: float) -> None:
    ids: set[str] = set()
    for f in final_dossiers():
        for p in json.loads(f.read_text(encoding="utf-8")).get("papers", []):
            aid = paper_arxiv_id(p)
            if aid:
                ids.add(aid)
    found: dict[str, dict] = json.loads(lookup_path.read_text(encoding="utf-8")) if lookup_path.exists() else {}
    todo = [x for x in sorted(ids) if x not in found]
    print(f"{len(ids)} arXiv ids referenced; {len(found)} already resolved; fetching {len(todo)}")
    for i in range(0, len(todo), batch_size):
        batch = todo[i : i + batch_size]
        url = f"https://export.arxiv.org/api/query?id_list={','.join(batch)}&max_results={len(batch)}"
        data = None
        for attempt in range(5):
            try:
                req = urllib.request.Request(url, headers={"User-Agent": "prebuilt-ai-models-bibliography-check/1.0"})
                with urllib.request.urlopen(req, timeout=90) as r:
                    data = r.read()
                break
            except urllib.error.HTTPError as e:
                wait = 45 * (attempt + 1)
                print(f"  batch {i // batch_size}: HTTP {e.code}; waiting {wait}s")
                time.sleep(wait)
            except Exception as e:  # noqa: BLE001
                print(f"  batch {i // batch_size}: {e}; waiting 30s")
                time.sleep(30)
        if data is None:
            print(f"  batch {i // batch_size}: giving up")
            continue
        root = ET.fromstring(data)
        for entry in root.findall("a:entry", NS):
            m = ID_RE.search(entry.findtext("a:id", default="", namespaces=NS))
            title = re.sub(r"\s+", " ", entry.findtext("a:title", default="", namespaces=NS)).strip()
            if not m or title.lower().startswith("error"):
                continue
            authors = [a.findtext("a:name", default="", namespaces=NS) for a in entry.findall("a:author", NS)]
            found[m.group(1)] = {
                "title": title,
                "first_author": authors[0] if authors else "",
                "n_authors": len(authors),
                "year": entry.findtext("a:published", default="", namespaces=NS)[:4],
            }
        lookup_path.write_text(json.dumps(found, indent=1, ensure_ascii=False), encoding="utf-8")
        print(f"  batch {i // batch_size}: resolved {len(found)} total")
        time.sleep(pause)
    print(f"done: {len(found)} of {len(ids)} resolved -> {lookup_path}")


def cmd_apply(lookup_path: Path, dry_run: bool) -> None:
    lookup: dict[str, dict] = json.loads(lookup_path.read_text(encoding="utf-8"))
    grand = {"verified": 0, "verified-corrected": 0, "unverified-nonarxiv": 0, "unverified-missing": 0, "unverified-mismatch": 0}
    for f in final_dossiers():
        d = json.loads(f.read_text(encoding="utf-8"))
        counts = dict.fromkeys(grand, 0)
        for p in d.get("papers", []):
            aid = paper_arxiv_id(p)
            if not aid:
                p["verification"] = "unverified"
                p.setdefault("verification_evidence", "no arXiv identifier; needs venue-page check")
                counts["unverified-nonarxiv"] += 1
                continue
            rec = lookup.get(aid)
            if rec is None:
                p["verification"] = "unverified"
                p["verification_evidence"] = f"arXiv {aid} not resolved by the metadata lookup"
                counts["unverified-missing"] += 1
                continue
            sim = similarity(p.get("title", ""), rec["title"])
            try:
                year_ok = abs(int(p.get("year") or 0) - int(rec["year"] or 0)) <= 1
            except ValueError:
                year_ok = False
            if sim >= 0.85 and year_ok:
                p["verification"] = "verified"
                p["verification_evidence"] = f"arXiv {aid}: title match {sim:.2f}, year {rec['year']}"
                counts["verified"] += 1
            elif sim >= 0.6:
                changes = []
                if sim < 0.97:
                    changes.append(f"title '{p.get('title')}' -> '{rec['title']}'")
                    p["title"] = rec["title"]
                if not year_ok:
                    changes.append(f"year {p.get('year')} -> {rec['year']}")
                    p["year"] = int(rec["year"])
                p["verification"] = "verified-corrected"
                p["verification_evidence"] = f"arXiv {aid}: " + ("; ".join(changes) or f"title match {sim:.2f}")
                counts["verified-corrected"] += 1
            else:
                p["verification"] = "unverified"
                p["verification_evidence"] = (
                    f"arXiv {aid} resolves to a different work ('{rec['title']}', {rec['year']}); id is probably wrong"
                )
                counts["unverified-mismatch"] += 1
        for k, v in counts.items():
            grand[k] += v
        d["_status"] = (
            "research + completeness critique; arXiv metadata verification applied "
            f"({counts['verified'] + counts['verified-corrected']} of {len(d.get('papers', []))} machine-verified; "
            "non-arXiv sources need a venue-page check)"
        )
        print(f"{f.stem}: {counts}")
        if not dry_run:
            f.write_text(json.dumps(d, indent=1, ensure_ascii=False), encoding="utf-8")
    print("total:", grand)


def main() -> None:
    ap = argparse.ArgumentParser(description=__doc__.split("\n")[0])
    sub = ap.add_subparsers(dest="cmd", required=True)
    f = sub.add_parser("fetch")
    f.add_argument("--lookup", type=Path, default=DEFAULT_LOOKUP)
    f.add_argument("--batch-size", type=int, default=25)
    f.add_argument("--pause", type=float, default=12.0)
    a = sub.add_parser("apply")
    a.add_argument("--lookup", type=Path, default=DEFAULT_LOOKUP)
    a.add_argument("--dry-run", action="store_true")
    args = ap.parse_args()
    if args.cmd == "fetch":
        cmd_fetch(args.lookup, args.batch_size, args.pause)
    else:
        cmd_apply(args.lookup, args.dry_run)


if __name__ == "__main__":
    main()

# Research dossiers

One JSON dossier per concept, produced by a three-stage literature workflow on
2026-10-11:

1. **Research** - an agent with web search and page fetch compiled sources for
   the concept (top-venue papers, highly cited preprints, authoritative
   engineering documentation), each with its key contribution and the design
   implication for a production implementation, plus implementable techniques
   with literature-backed default parameters, architecture recommendations,
   pitfalls, evaluation metrics, engineering-adaptation notes and composition
   notes.
2. **Critique** - a second agent audited the dossier for missing seminal work
   and factual errors, adding verified sources and recording corrections.
3. **Verify** - citation verifiers checked every paper against its arXiv or
   venue page (existence, metadata, faithfulness of the claimed contribution).
   Unverifiable entries were dropped; corrected metadata is marked
   `verification: "verified-corrected"`.

Files:

| File | Meaning |
| --- | --- |
| `<concept>.json` | Final dossier after critique and verification. Source of truth for citations. |
| `<concept>.draft.json` | Snapshot after stage 1 only. Kept for provenance; superseded by the final file. |

Concepts: `hybrid-retrieval`, `task-decomposition`, `answer-verification`,
`parallelization`, `caching`, `pipeline-rag`, and the cross-cutting
`prompting-techniques` and `pipeline-architecture`.

`python tools/build_bibliography.py` renders all final dossiers into
[`../RESEARCH_BIBLIOGRAPHY.md`](../RESEARCH_BIBLIOGRAPHY.md).

Dossier schema (abridged):

```json
{
  "concept": "...",
  "summary": "state-of-the-art summary",
  "papers": [{"title", "authors", "year", "venue", "url", "arxiv_id", "citation_signal", "key_contribution", "design_implication", "verification"}],

  "engineering_adaptation_notes": ["..."],
  "composition_notes": ["..."],
  "critique_corrections": ["..."],
  "dropped_papers": [{"title", "reason"}]
}
```

"""Cross-check README citations against the research dossiers.

For every ``*.md`` under the model folders (plus ``docs/COMPOSITION_PATTERNS.md``
and the root ``README.md``), find citation-like fragments - italicised titles
(``*Title*``) on lines that look like citations, arXiv URLs and arXiv
identifiers - and confirm each one appears in some dossier in
``docs/research/``. Titles are matched case-insensitively after normalising
punctuation; a title counts as present if it equals a dossier title, is a
prefix of one (or vice versa), or is at least 85% similar after stripping a
trailing alias such as "(RankGPT)".

Exit status is non-zero when an unknown citation is found, so this can run in CI::

    python tools/check_citations.py            # report
    python tools/check_citations.py --strict   # also fail on titles found only in draft dossiers
"""
from __future__ import annotations

import argparse
import difflib
import json
import re
import sys
from pathlib import Path

ROOT = Path(__file__).resolve().parents[1]
RESEARCH_DIR = ROOT / "docs" / "research"
MODEL_FOLDERS = [
    "hybrid_retrieval_model",
    "task_decomposition_model",
    "answer_verification_model",
    "parallelization_model",
    "caching_model",
    "pipeline_rag_model",
]

# single-asterisk italics with non-space edges; never **bold**
ITALIC_TITLE = re.compile(r"(?<!\*)\*(?=\S)([^*\n]{12,200}?)(?<=\S)\*(?!\*)")
ARXIV_URL = re.compile(r"arxiv\.org/(?:abs|pdf)/(\d{4}\.\d{4,5})")
ARXIV_ID = re.compile(r"\barXiv:(\d{4}\.\d{4,5})")
# a line must look like a citation (year in parentheses, "et al.", a URL or arXiv) before its italics are checked
CITATION_LINE = re.compile(r"\(\d{4}[a-z]?\)|et al\.|https?://|arXiv")
# strip trailing aliases such as "(RankGPT)" or "(vLLM)"
ALIAS_SUFFIX = re.compile(r"\s*\((?:[A-Za-z0-9+\-/ .]{2,40})\)\s*$")


def norm(s: str) -> str:
    s = s.lower().replace("×", "x")
    s = re.sub(r"[‘’“”'\"`]", "", s)
    s = re.sub(r"[^a-z0-9]+", " ", s)
    return s.strip()


def load_known() -> tuple[set[str], set[str], set[str]]:
    final_titles: set[str] = set()
    draft_titles: set[str] = set()
    ids: set[str] = set()
    for f in RESEARCH_DIR.glob("*.json"):
        if f.name == "arxiv_lookup.json":
            continue
        d = json.loads(f.read_text(encoding="utf-8"))
        target = draft_titles if f.name.endswith(".draft.json") else final_titles
        for p in d.get("papers", []):
            target.add(norm(p.get("title", "")))
            venue = p.get("venue") or ""
            if "also known as:" in venue:  # alternate titles recorded during verification
                target.add(norm(venue.split("also known as:", 1)[1]))
            aid = p.get("arxiv_id") or ""
            m = re.search(r"(\d{4}\.\d{4,5})", aid) or ARXIV_URL.search(p.get("url", ""))
            if m:
                ids.add(m.group(1))
    return final_titles, draft_titles, ids


def title_known(t: str, known: set[str]) -> bool:
    for candidate in (t, ALIAS_SUFFIX.sub("", t)):
        n = norm(candidate)
        if not n:
            continue
        if n in known:
            return True
        if len(n) < 12:
            continue
        for k in known:
            if k.startswith(n) or n.startswith(k):
                return True
            if difflib.SequenceMatcher(None, n, k).ratio() >= 0.85:
                return True
    return False


def scan(path: Path, final_titles: set[str], draft_titles: set[str], ids: set[str]) -> list[str]:
    text = path.read_text(encoding="utf-8", errors="replace")
    lines = text.splitlines()
    problems: list[str] = []
    for m in ITALIC_TITLE.finditer(text):
        t = m.group(1).strip()
        if len(t.split()) < 2:
            continue
        line = text.count("\n", 0, m.start()) + 1
        if not CITATION_LINE.search(lines[line - 1]):
            continue  # italic emphasis in prose, not a citation
        if title_known(t, final_titles):
            continue
        if title_known(t, draft_titles):
            problems.append(f"{path.relative_to(ROOT)}:{line}: title only in DRAFT dossier: {t!r}")
        else:
            problems.append(f"{path.relative_to(ROOT)}:{line}: title not found in any dossier: {t!r}")
    for rx in (ARXIV_URL, ARXIV_ID):
        for m in rx.finditer(text):
            if m.group(1) not in ids:
                line = text.count("\n", 0, m.start()) + 1
                problems.append(f"{path.relative_to(ROOT)}:{line}: arXiv id {m.group(1)} not in any dossier")
    return problems


def main() -> int:
    ap = argparse.ArgumentParser()
    ap.add_argument("--strict", action="store_true", help="fail on titles found only in draft dossiers")
    args = ap.parse_args()
    final_titles, draft_titles, ids = load_known()
    files = [ROOT / "README.md", ROOT / "docs" / "COMPOSITION_PATTERNS.md"]
    for folder in MODEL_FOLDERS:
        files += sorted((ROOT / folder).rglob("*.md"))
    problems: list[str] = []
    for f in files:
        if f.exists():
            problems += scan(f, final_titles, draft_titles, ids)
    hard = [p for p in problems if "not found" in p or "not in any dossier" in p]
    soft = [p for p in problems if p not in hard]
    for p in problems:
        print(p)
    print(f"\nchecked {len(files)} files: {len(hard)} unknown citation(s), {len(soft)} draft-only citation(s)")
    if hard or (args.strict and soft):
        return 1
    return 0


if __name__ == "__main__":
    sys.exit(main())

        target = draft_titles if f.name.endswith(".draft.json") else final_titles
        for p in d.get("papers", []):

            venue = p.get("venue") or ""

                target.add(norm(venue.split("also known as:", 1)[1]))
            aid = p.get("arxiv_id") or ""

    soft = [p for p in problems if p not in hard]
    for p in problems:
        print(p)
    print(f"\nchecked {len(files)} files: {len(hard)} unknown citation(s), {len(soft)} draft-only citation(s)")
    if hard or (args.strict and soft):
        return 1
    return 0


if __name__ == "__main__":
    sys.exit(main())

"""Cross-check README citations against the research dossiers.

For every ``*.md`` under the model folders (and ``docs/COMPOSITION_PATTERNS.md``,
the main ``README.md``), find citation-like fragments - italicised titles
(``*Title*``), arXiv URLs and arXiv identifiers - and confirm each one appears
in some dossier in ``docs/research/``. Titles are matched case-insensitively
after normalising punctuation; a title counts as present if it matches a
dossier paper title exactly or if one is a prefix of the other (handles
subtitles).

Exit status is non-zero when an unknown citation is found, so this can run in CI::

    python tools/check_citations.py            # report
    python tools/check_citations.py --strict   # also fail on titles found only in draft dossiers
"""
from __future__ import annotations

import argparse
import json
import re
import sys
from pathlib import Path

ROOT = Path(__file__).resolve().parents[1]
RESEARCH_DIR = ROOT / "docs" / "research"
MODEL_FOLDERS = [
    "hybrid_retrieval_model",
    "task_decomposition_model",
    "answer_verification_model",
    "parallelization_model",
    "caching_model",
    "pipeline_rag_model",
]

ITALIC_TITLE = re.compile(r"(?<!\*)\*(?=\S)([^*
]{12,200}?)(?<=\S)\*(?!\*)")  # single-asterisk italics, non-space edges
ARXIV_URL = re.compile(r"arxiv\.org/(?:abs|pdf)/(\d{4}\.\d{4,5})")
ARXIV_ID = re.compile(r"\barXiv:(\d{4}\.\d{4,5})")


def norm(s: str) -> str:
    s = s.lower().replace("×", "x")
    s = re.sub(r"[‘’“”'\"`]", "", s)
    s = re.sub(r"[^a-z0-9]+", " ", s)
    return s.strip()


def load_known(include_drafts: bool) -> tuple[set[str], set[str], set[str]]:
    final_titles: set[str] = set()
    draft_titles: set[str] = set()
    ids: set[str] = set()
    for f in RESEARCH_DIR.glob("*.json"):
        d = json.loads(f.read_text(encoding="utf-8"))
        target = draft_titles if f.name.endswith(".draft.json") else final_titles
        for p in d.get("papers", []):
            target.add(norm(p.get("title", "")))
            aid = p.get("arxiv_id") or ""
            m = re.search(r"(\d{4}\.\d{4,5})", aid) or ARXIV_URL.search(p.get("url", ""))
            if m:
                ids.add(m.group(1))
    if include_drafts:
        final_titles |= draft_titles
    return final_titles, draft_titles, ids


def title_known(t: str, known: set[str]) -> bool:
    import difflib

    candidates = [t, ALIAS_SUFFIX.sub("", t)]
    for c in candidates:
        n = norm(c)
        if not n:
            continue
        if n in known:
            return True
        for k in known:
            if len(n) >= 12 and (k.startswith(n) or n.startswith(k)):
                return True
            if len(n) >= 12 and difflib.SequenceMatcher(None, n, k).ratio() >= 0.85:
                return True
    return False


def scan(path: Path, final_titles: set[str], draft_titles: set[str], ids: set[str]) -> list[str]:
    text = path.read_text(encoding="utf-8", errors="replace")
    problems: list[str] = []
    for m in ITALIC_TITLE.finditer(text):
        t = m.group(1).strip()
        # skip emphasis that is clearly not a title
        if t.lower() in ("verified", "not independently verified") or len(t.split()) < 3:
            continue
        line = text.count("\n", 0, m.start()) + 1
        if title_known(t, final_titles):
            continue
        if title_known(t, draft_titles):
            problems.append(f"{path.relative_to(ROOT)}:{line}: title only in DRAFT dossier: {t!r}")
        else:
            problems.append(f"{path.relative_to(ROOT)}:{line}: title not found in any dossier: {t!r}")
    for rx in (ARXIV_URL, ARXIV_ID):
        for m in rx.finditer(text):
            if m.group(1) not in ids:
                line = text.count("\n", 0, m.start()) + 1
                problems.append(f"{path.relative_to(ROOT)}:{line}: arXiv id {m.group(1)} not in any dossier")
    return problems


def main() -> int:
    ap = argparse.ArgumentParser()
    ap.add_argument("--strict", action="store_true", help="fail on titles found only in draft dossiers")
    args = ap.parse_args()
    final_titles, draft_titles, ids = load_known(include_drafts=False)
    files = [ROOT / "README.md", ROOT / "docs" / "COMPOSITION_PATTERNS.md"]
    for folder in MODEL_FOLDERS:
        files += sorted((ROOT / folder).rglob("*.md"))
    problems: list[str] = []
    for f in files:
        if f.exists():
            problems += scan(f, final_titles, draft_titles, ids)
    hard = [p for p in problems if "not found" in p or "not in any dossier" in p]
    soft = [p for p in problems if p not in hard]
    for p in problems:
        print(p)
    print(f"\nchecked {len(files)} files: {len(hard)} unknown citation(s), {len(soft)} draft-only citation(s)")
    if hard or (args.strict and soft):
        return 1
    return 0


if __name__ == "__main__":
    sys.exit(main())

## 6. Known limitations and roadmap

Recorded by the package engineers as `core_change_requests` during implementation; none blocks use of the models today.

| Area | Limitation | Planned change |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `RunContext` budgets | `llm_call()` checks the remaining call budget before each call, but N concurrent callers can all pass the check before any completes, so a fan-out can overshoot `max_llm_calls` by up to the fan-out width. The task decomposition scheduler reserves calls per wave locally to compensate. | Add `BudgetTracker.try_reserve(n)` / `ctx.reserve_calls(n)` so fan-outs claim budget atomically up front. |
| `MockLLM` structured stubs | `example_from_schema` emits arrays with `minItems` elements (usually zero), so offline runs exercise the heuristic fallbacks more than the LLM-planned branches. name: feedback-workflow-session-limits
description: Lessons from running large multi-agent Workflow runs in this project: session limits cut off parallel agents, resume cache breaks under parallel ordering, so stage work and checkpoint to disk
metadata:

---

Running 6-8 heavy implementation agents in one Workflow repeatedly hit the account's session usage limit mid-run (2026-10-11/12); every unfinished agent was lost, and `resumeFromRunId` re-ran completed critique agents because the cache matches the *prefix of agent() calls in invocation order*, which parallel pipelines do not preserve.

**Why:** Workflow results only persist when an agent finishes; partial reasoning is lost, but files the agent already wrote to disk survive.

**How to apply:** For long builds in this repo, (1) split into small staged workflows (implement -> review -> fix -> integrate) and launch the next stage only after inspecting results; (2) tell agents to write a working checkpoint (model.py + smoke test) early and to resume from existing files; (3) keep concurrency to about three heavy agents per stage; (4) save intermediate structured results (reviews, dossiers) to the scratchpad or docs/ so a later stage can read them from disk instead of re-running. Related: [[project-prebuilt-ai-models-architecture]].

class ReentrantExecutor:
    """``Executor`` facade over one ``ParallelExecutor`` that is safe to nest and shows up in the trace.

    Friction: ``ParallelExecutor.map`` takes Bulkhead slots from one ``default`` pool. The
    decomposition scheduler holds a slot per sub-task while each sub-task's RAG run (retrieval
    fan-out) and verifier (sample fan-out) wait for slots from the same pool, which deadlocks
    once the outer wave fills the pool. This facade routes each nesting level to its own
    bulkhead resource (``tier0``, ``tier1`` ...) through ``map_outcomes(resource=...)``, so the
    rate limiter, retry budget, breaker and stats stay shared while nested fan-outs cannot
    starve each other. It also opens a span, which the direct API does not.
    """

    def __init__(self, inner: ParallelExecutor, tracer: Tracer) -> None:
        self.inner = inner
        self.tracer = tracer

    def stats(self):  # type: ignore[no-untyped-def]
        return self.inner.stats

content.thinking: Integration testing found two cross-package issues: nested fan-outs can deadlock on the single default bulkhead, and `Verdict` doesn't carry usage data, causing verification cost to drop from roll-ups. I'll pass the deadlock fix to the parallelization fixer and handle the `Verdict` fix myself.

input.message: One more defect to fix in parallelization, found by the integration example (examples/enterprise_pipeline.py, class ReentrantExecutor, read its docstring): ParallelExecutor.map takes Bulkhead slots from a single "default" pool. When an outer map (decomposition waves) holds every slot and each task inside it calls executor.map again (RAG retrieval fan-out, verifier sampling), the inner calls wait on the same pool forever: a deadlock. Make nested map/gather calls on the same executor safe by default, e.g. track nesting depth with a contextvars.ContextVar and route each nesting level to its own bulkhead resource (or bypass the bulkhead for nested calls) while keeping the shared rate limiter, retry budget, breaker and stats. Add a regression test (outer map with max_concurrency=2 over 4 items, each calling executor.map over 3 items, must complete under a timeout), document it in the README, and keep everything else passing.      - Plain `Verifier` objects still use `verify()` plus `details["usage"]`.
     - I did not edit `answer_verification`. Tests cover a cost-incurring fake component and the real `AnswerVerificationModel`.
  4. **`retrieval_trigger_threshold` did nothing:** `HopStep` has a new `need_probability` field. A hop retrieves with its `next_query` when that value is above the threshold, even if the model says it can answer. This is recorded as `triggered_by="retrieval_trigger"`. The test shows thresholds 0.2 and 0.6 behaving differently.
  5. **`contextual_prefix='llm'` did nothing:** each chunk now gets one `CONTEXT_PREFIX_PROMPT` call, once per index. It is online only, budget-guarded, and has bounded concurrency. Chunks that already have an LLM prefix are skipped, and a new `llm_prefix_max_chunks` setting (default 200) caps the cost.

  - **`constraints.deterministic`:** every advisory stage uses its heuristic. Generation is the only LLM call, once per Self-Route pass. This is documented in the README.
  - **Retrieval cache:** retrievers without a `version` are keyed by identity plus a cache epoch. There is a new `invalidate_retrieval_cache()`, and the first cache error per model is surfaced as a warning.

    - The precedence bug in `test_rag_model.py:138` is fixed with parentheses.

Removing them makes the README meet the stricter rule in ARCHITECTURE 3.5 that a model cites only its own dossier (`pipeline-rag.json`). Their claims now cite Asai et al. (2024) and Gao et al. (2023) ALCE, or Greshake et al. (2023) alone for the prompt-injection point.

The final verifier was also rejecting the markdown headings in the composed answer (`# <task>`, `## t1: Check the corrosion allowance`). It covered: `strip_volatile` defaulting to False, `ttl_s<=0` meaning "do not retain", `peek()`, FileBackend re-tagging, `fut.exception()`, `confirm_hit` and the embedder-mismatch guard. One existing test was failing because of it. I kept that work, connected it to the code that needed it, and added tests.
  
  ### Critical and major fixes (each has a regression test)
  - **Exact key merged different questions (critical).** Bare timestamps, clock times, UUIDs and hex ids are now kept in the key; only labelled tracing ids (`request_id: ...`) are stripped. The old normalisation test is updated, and new tests check key differences at both the key and the client level.
  - **`ttl_s=0` crashed the hot path.** The middleware, `execute()` and `CacheStore` now treat 0 as "do not store", warn, and never raise. `CachePlan.ttl_s` stays `ge=0` with 0 documented as "do not retain", so an LLM plan returning 0 still validates. I also guarded against a non-numeric `cache_ttl_s`.
  - **`plan()` failed on LLM errors.** Any `LLMError` (refusal, truncation, connection error) or `ValidationError` now falls back to the heuristic plan with a warning. `BudgetExceededError` still propagates.
  - **`bump_version` didn't touch the exact tier.**
    - It now purges the namespace tag (`ns:<namespace>`) from both tiers and logs how many exact entries it removed.
    - Entries in both tiers are stamped with the namespace version.
    - Wrapped clients share the version registry and reject (and drop) entries written under an older version.
  - **Verification calls were invisible to budgets.** The equivalence check's usage is now added to the response the caller receives, so `RunContext` budgets and the tracer see it. New metrics `verification_calls` and `verification_cost_usd` track it, and its cost is subtracted from `cost_saved_usd`. Swallowed errors are now logged, and `BudgetExceededError` is re-raised.
  - **Malformed stored values crashed the client.**
    - `execute()` now stores `inputs["response"]` as an `LLMResponse`.
    - Any stored value that isn't a valid response is dropped, counted in `corrupt_entries`, and treated as a miss instead of raising.
    - CachingModel and the wrapped client now build keys from the same model id, so a response stored through `run()` is actually served by a client wrapping the same model.
  - **Shared client ignored the request's domain.** `metadata["domain"]` now picks the profile per request, so one shared client still disables the semantic tier for safety-critical requests. An unknown domain keeps the profile the client was wrapped with rather than falling back to the more permissive `general` rules.
  
  ### Minors and spec gaps fixed
  - Over-eager planner word lists (roll, unique, alternatives, address, me, status, personal and similar) now only trigger inside phrases.
  - `embedding_dimension` is actually used now.
  - The tenant salt is shown only as a hash in namespaces and reports.
  - `run()` no longer skews the backend's hit/miss stats.
  - Corrected TTL advice: 1h for gaps up to 60 minutes once the prefix has been used 3 times, and keep-alive only when it's cheaper.
  - JSON with unsorted keys in a constant prompt is now an informational note, not an invalidator; I also deleted the dead code next to it.
  - Semantic hit counts only rise when a hit is actually served.
  - The wrapped client now requests the 1-hour provider TTL when the plan recommends it (`apply_prefix_ttl`).
  - It also prewarms the provider prefix once for requests marked `fan_out` (only for clients that support prewarm; concurrent callers wait for it).
  - Test-quality fixes: replaced the vacuous assertion, made the SQLite eviction assertion exact, isolated the CLI environment variable with monkeypatch, and corrected the docstring that claimed `cache_hits` appears in the result.
  
  ### README and citations
  - Fixed: the stale note saying `caching.json` didn't exist, the CLI flags, the fallback and `bump_version` descriptions, the domain/deterministic metadata and the core limitation, the config rows (`strip_labelled_ids`, `strip_volatile=False`, `apply_prefix_ttl`, `embedding_dimension`, TTL rules), the `key_for` docs, the test counts, and the `low` effort for planning documented as a deviation from ARCHITECTURE 3.2.
  - Every short title alias (*GPTCache*, *ARC*, *TinyLFU* and the rest) is now the exact title from the dossier with its URL, so the checker actually validates them. TinyLFU's year is corrected to 2015, and the OpenTelemetry citation now has a title.
  
  ### Where the review was wrong or I didn't follow it
  - **Schluntz & Zhang, FrugalGPT and OpenTelemetry citations:** the review says they aren't in `caching.json`. That's true, but they are in `pipeline-architecture.json`, which your rules allow, so I kept them with exact titles. ARCHITECTURE 3.5 alone would forbid them.
  - **"Summarize the quarterly report" classed as cacheable:** left unchanged. The exact key covers a report that's in the prompt, and the dependency fingerprint covers one passed as context.
  - **"Lower confidence on one weak term":** not done, because the ambiguous single-word triggers were removed instead.
  - **Folding the embedder id into the namespace:** not done. Semantic lookup already skips entries made by a different embedder or dimension, so swapping embedders produces a miss, not an error.
  
  ### Changes needed in `pipeline_core` (outside my folder)
  1. `RunContext.llm_call` should copy `constraints.deterministic` and `request.domain` into `LLMRequest.metadata`. Until it does, calling components have to set them.
  2. `_max_usage` should merge `cache_hits`.
  
  Both are documented in the README.
  
  One leftover: `python -m caching.evaluation` prints a harmless runpy RuntimeWarning, because `caching/__init__.py` imports the evaluation module. I didn't change it.
  
  Files changed are in `C:/Users/kenne/Documents/Prebuilt AI Technique Models/caching_model/`:
  - `caching/`: `middleware.py`, `model.py`, `plan.py`, `prefix.py`, `invalidation.py`, `semantic.py`, `__init__.py`
  - `README.md`
  - `tests/`: `test_backends_keys.py`, `test_semantic_prefix_invalidation.py`, `test_middleware_model.py`, and the new `test_review_regressions.py`

from __future__ import annotations

SIMPLE = ep.DEMO_TASKS[0]["task"]
COMPLEX = ep.DEMO_TASKS[1]["task"]
ALL_COMPONENTS = {"hybrid_retrieval", "task_decomposition", "answer_verification", "parallelization", "caching", "pipeline_rag"}


def make_pipeline(**kwargs) -> ep.EnterprisePipeline:  # type: ignore[no-untyped-def]
    pipeline = ep.build_pipeline(offline=True, tracer=Tracer(name="test"), **kwargs)
    pipeline.index(ep.CORPUS)
    return pipeline


@pytest.fixture(scope="module")
def pipeline() -> ep.EnterprisePipeline:
    return make_pipeline()


@pytest.fixture(scope="module")
def simple_result(pipeline: ep.EnterprisePipeline):  # type: ignore[no-untyped-def]

@pytest.fixture(scope="module")
def complex_result(pipeline: ep.EnterprisePipeline):  # type: ignore[no-untyped-def]
    return pipeline.run_sync(TaskRequest(task=COMPLEX, domain="mechanical_engineering"))

def test_components_satisfy_protocols(pipeline: ep.EnterprisePipeline) -> None:
    assert isinstance(pipeline.retrieval, Retriever) and isinstance(pipeline.retriever, Retriever)
    assert isinstance(pipeline.verification, Verifier) and isinstance(pipeline.verifier, Verifier)
    assert isinstance(pipeline.parallel.executor, Executor) and isinstance(pipeline.executor, Executor)
    assert isinstance(pipeline.caching, ResponseCache) and isinstance(pipeline.cache, ResponseCache)
    assert isinstance(pipeline.decomposition.solver, ep.RAGSubTaskSolver)  # SubTaskSolver callable
    assert pipeline.rag.retriever is pipeline.retriever and pipeline.rag.verifier is pipeline.verifier and pipeline.rag.executor is pipeline.executor
    assert pipeline.rag.cache is pipeline.caching.cache
    assert pipeline.decomposition.executor is pipeline.executor and pipeline.decomposition.verifier is pipeline.verifier

    client = pipeline.llm
    assert isinstance(client, ep.CachedLLMClient)
    assert isinstance(client, MockLLM), "offline detection (RunContext.offline) must survive the cache wrapper"
    assert client.backend is pipeline.caching.backend
    for name, component in pipeline.components.items():
        if name == "caching":

content.text:
All six models are built and documented, and they run together end to end. The full quality gate passes offline: 727 tests, every package's command-line tool, all 13 example scripts, the static API-rule checks, and the citation check. Nothing has been run against the real Claude API, because this machine has no credentials. Everything was verified with the built-in offline mock, which proves wiring and control flow but not answer quality.

| Folder | Tests passing |
| --- | ---: |
| Shared core (`common/`) | 27 |
| Hybrid retrieval | 129 |
| Task decomposition | 94 |
| Answer verification | 99 |
| Parallelization | 117 |
| Caching | 118 |
| Pipeline RAG | 131 |
| Six-model integration example | 12 |

**What you have**
- **Six model folders**, each with code, tests, two runnable examples, a command-line tool and a README. Each README covers how the model reasons about a prompt, every setting with the paper that justifies its default, how to adapt it to an engineering domain, and how it was built.
- **How each model reasons:** every model first reads the natural-language task and picks a strategy (a "plan"), then carries it out. Without credentials, it falls back to rule-based planning.
- **Adapting to engineering work:** this happens through domain profiles. Eight ship (software, mechanical, electrical, civil, systems, data, chemical and general), and adding one changes retrieval weights, verification rules and acceptance thresholds across all six models.
- **A main [README.md](README.md)** explains how the models combine into one pipeline: cache first, route by complexity, decompose, run in parallel, retrieve, generate with citations, verify. [examples/enterprise_pipeline.py](examples/enterprise_pipeline.py) wires all six together on a sample pump-station corpus.
- **Research:** 456 sources across the six models plus prompting and pipeline architecture. 382 were confirmed against arXiv records. The other 74 have no arXiv entry (books, standards, vendor documentation) and are marked as not independently verified. READMEs cite only listed sources, and a script enforces that.

**Process.** Each model went through an independent adversarial review and a fix pass. Combining the models exposed several real cross-model bugs, which are now fixed:
- nested parallel work could deadlock;
- verification cost disappeared from cost totals;
- wrapping the client in the cache hid offline mode from the other models;
- decomposition sent its own final check to retrieval, which had nothing to retrieve and dragged confidence from about 0.7 down to 0.18.

**Known limits**, listed in [docs/ARCHITECTURE.md](docs/ARCHITECTURE.md):
- When many calls run at once, the call budget can be overshot by the number of parallel calls, and the cost limit is only checked after each call.
- The offline mock exercises the rule-based paths more than the Claude-driven ones.
- The folder is not a git repository, so nothing has been committed.

To check everything yourself:
```bash
python tools/quality_gate.py
```

The next step is a live run with `ANTHROPIC_API_KEY` set, to measure real answer quality and cost.

entries.description:
The account's Claude Code plan limits and how full a session's context window is.

`plan`: the limits the app's usage card shows (5-hour, weekly, per-model weekly, extra usage) with percent used and reset time. Status "not_applicable" means plan limits do not apply here (an API key, Bedrock, Vertex or a gateway); "unavailable" means they could not be read now, and the note says whether asking again helps. `context` (session_id, default "self"): that session's window as the composer shows it — tokens used, percent, where auto-compact starts, the largest categories; read from the session's own process, so an idle, starting or archived session reports it unavailable.

For pacing side sessions and deciding when to wrap up, compact or hand off. Read-only.

session_id.description: Whose context window to report: a sessionId from list_sessions, or the literal string "self" (the default) for this session. The plan limits are the account's either way.

import json, pathlib, glob
root = pathlib.Path("05a19eb0-51c5-4be5-a66e-6d8ba4e1b8d4")

def sum_usage(path):
    t = {"input":0,"output":0,"cache_read":0,"cache_write":0,"msgs":0}
    seen=set()
    for line in open(path, encoding="utf-8", errors="replace"):
        try: r=json.loads(line)

        m=r.get("message") or {}
        u=m.get("usage") if isinstance(m,dict) else None
        if not u: continue
        mid=m.get("id")
        if mid in seen: continue
        seen.add(mid)
        t["input"]+=u.get("input_tokens",0) or 0
        t["output"]+=u.get("output_tokens",0) or 0
        t["cache_read"]+=u.get("cache_read_input_tokens",0) or 0
        t["cache_write"]+=u.get("cache_creation_input_tokens",0) or 0
        t["msgs"]+=1
    return t

print("SUB", tot)

## Push status

I couldn't finish the push. The repository `KennethLei1492/prebuilt-ai-technique-models` doesn't exist yet. Creating one needs your GitHub login, and this machine has no GitHub CLI or authorized GitHub connector.

Everything else is ready:
- **Local git repository** in the project folder, with one commit of 216 files.
- **Remote:** already pointed at `https://github.com/KennethLei1492/prebuilt-ai-technique-models.git`.
- **Secret scan:** nothing found, and caches and `.env` files are ignored.

To finish:
1. Create an empty repository at github.com/new named `prebuilt-ai-technique-models`. Leave the README, .gitignore and license boxes unchecked. Private or public is your choice.
2. Run this in the project folder. Git Credential Manager will open a browser sign-in the first time.

```bash
git push -u origin main
```

If you'd like me to push it myself next time, install GitHub CLI and run `gh auth login`.

## How to use the models

Set up once from the project folder:

```bash
pip install -e ".[dev,retrieval]"
```

```bash
python tools/quality_gate.py
```

With `ANTHROPIC_API_KEY` set, the models call Claude (`claude-opus-5-5` by default). Without it they run offline on a built-in mock, which is useful for trying the wiring but not for real answers.

**Use one model on its own.** Each folder works independently from the command line or from Python:

```bash
python -m pipeline_rag --domain mechanical_engineering "What corrosion allowance does the specification require for the pump casing?"
```

Every model has `run(task)` for the full plan-then-execute cycle, plus a direct method for programmatic use:

| Model | Direct method | Use it for |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Hybrid Retrieval | `retrieve(query, k=10)` | Finding the most relevant passages in your documents |
| Task Decomposition | `decompose(task)` | Breaking a multi-part request into ordered sub-tasks |
| Answer Verification | `verify(answer, task=..., evidence=...)` | Checking an answer against sources, units and domain rules |
| Parallelization | `executor.map(fn, items)` | Running many calls at once with rate limits and retries |
| Caching | `wrap(llm)` | Avoiding paying twice for the same or similar request |
| Pipeline RAG | `answer(question, documents)` | Cited answers from a document set |

**Use all six together.** This is the recommended way. `EnterprisePipeline` in [examples/enterprise_pipeline.py](examples/enterprise_pipeline.py) wires them into one pipeline:

```python
import sys; sys.path.insert(0, "examples")
from enterprise_pipeline import EnterprisePipeline

pipe = EnterprisePipeline(domain="mechanical_engineering")
pipe.index(documents)   # list of {"id", "text", "metadata"} or plain strings
result = pipe.run_sync("Check the NPSH margin against API 610 and list open risks from the trip report.")
print(result.status, result.confidence, result.output_text)
```

Simple questions go straight to retrieval-augmented generation. Complex ones are split into sub-tasks that run in parallel, and every answer is verified before it's returned. Branch on `result.status`: `SUCCESS`, `NEEDS_REVIEW` (confidence below the domain's threshold, so a person should check it), `PARTIAL`, `FAILED` or `CACHED`.

**Adapt it to your field** by registering a domain profile with your units, standards, verification rules and risk level. All six models change behaviour with no code edits. The "Adapting to any task" section of the main [README.md](README.md) shows how.

## Tokens and agents used

These numbers come from the session transcripts.

| | Model calls | Output tokens | Total tokens processed |
| --- | ---: | ---: | ---: |
| Main session | 121 | 251,363 | 42.1 million |
| Subagents | 1,032 | 1,951,585 | 163.5 million |
| **Total** | **1,153** | **2.2 million** | **205.7 million** |

Most of the 205.7 million is cache reads: 187.6 million tokens of context re-read at about one-tenth the normal price. Fresh input was only about 24,000 tokens, and cache writes were 15.8 million.

**Agents:** 111 were launched in total, across seven multi-agent workflow runs plus four individually delegated fixers. Of those, 103 did work. Only 49 finished their assignment cleanly. The rest were cut off when the account hit its usage limit several times. Their files on disk were kept and finished by later agents, which is why the agent count is higher than a single clean run would need.

**Your plan usage right now:** 14% of the 5-hour window, 44% of the weekly all-models limit, and 83% of the weekly Fable limit.

tools.description:
Launch a new agent to handle complex, multi-step tasks. Each agent type has specific capabilities and tools available to it.

Available agent types are listed in <system-reminder> messages in the conversation.

When using the Agent tool, specify a subagent_type parameter to select which agent type to use. If omitted, the general-purpose agent is used.

## When to use

A fresh agent costs more than it looks. It knows only what you put in the prompt, and you see only the summary it sends back — both handoffs drop detail, and neither of you can tell what the other missed. You can't watch it work, only wait or cancel. Its mistakes come back in the same confident register as its findings, and an agent handed your hypothesis tends to return it confirmed. Several at once spend tokens in a burst the user didn't ask for. Weigh those tokens against the accuracy they buy: the user pays for agents you did not need, and pays again for work you redo because you skipped one.

Reach for this when you have independent work to run in parallel, when the user asks for a side quest that shouldn't block your main thread, or when answering would mean reading across several files — delegate that and you keep the conclusion, not the file dumps.

Do the work yourself when it is a handful of tool calls or a lookup whose target you already know; don't delegate a check you could run inline. Delegate review only when you want a read that isn't anchored on yours — then give it the code, not your conclusion. Once you've delegated something, don't also run it yourself; wait for the result. When in doubt, don't spawn.

When you do spawn one, brief it like the peer it is: state the goal and what you have already ruled out, point it at the files and docs worth reading instead of retyping them, and keep the scope explicit and narrow. That brief is the only context it will have, so it is your one lever on every cost above — and if you cannot write a clear one, you do not understand the task well enough to hand it off.

- The agent's final report is not shown to the user — relay what matters.
- Use SendMessage with the agent's ID or name to continue a previously spawned agent with its context intact; a new Agent call starts fresh.
- Each agent type's model, reasoning effort, and tools come from its definition (`.claude/agents/*.md` frontmatter or SDK `agents`).
- `isolation: "worktree"` gives the agent its own git worktree (auto-cleaned if unchanged).
- Subagents run in the background by default; you'll be notified when one completes. Pass `run_in_background: false` only when your very next action depends on the result and nothing else could usefully happen while it runs — otherwise background it so the user can interject. Never fabricate or predict a pending agent's results — the notification is never something you write yourself; if the user asks before it arrives, say it's still running.

description.description: A short (3-5 word) description of the task

prompt.description: The task for the agent to perform

subagent_type.description: The type of specialized agent to use for this task

model.description: Optional model override for this agent. Takes precedence over the agent definition's model frontmatter and the configured default subagent model. If omitted, uses the agent definition's model, else the default (inherits from the parent unless a default subagent model is configured). Ignored for subagent_type: "fork" — forks always inherit the parent model.

effort.description: Reasoning effort for this agent. Set this ONLY when the user, or instructions such as CLAUDE.md or a skill, explicitly ask that this agent or delegated work run at a specific effort level, never on your own judgment; otherwise omit it and the agent runs at its usual effort.

run_in_background.description: Agents run in the background by default; you will be notified when one completes. Set to false only when your very next action depends on this agent's result and nothing else could usefully happen while it runs — otherwise leave it in the background so the user can hand you other work.

isolation.description: Isolation mode. "worktree" creates a temporary git worktree so the agent works on an isolated copy of the repo. "remote" launches the agent in a remote cloud environment (always runs in background; availability is gated).
